name: Sprocket
text: To improve our self-improvement process, I recommend that we prioritize reviewing our prompts and engines first, as this will allow us to identify and address any biases or inaccuracies that may be affecting our overall performance. By focusing on these areas, we can ensure that our routing and code are working with the best possible inputs, making our efforts more efficient and effective. This decision means we'll be accepting the trade-off of potentially delaying other tasks, such as reviewing our own code, but I believe this is worth it to lay a strong foundation for our improvement efforts. By doing so, we'll be able to make more informed decisions and apply safe changes that have a greater impact.

name: Gauge
text: I'm not convinced that reviewing prompts and engines first is the best approach, as it may not address the underlying issues with our routing and code that could be causing the most significant problems. A better alternative might be to start by analyzing our error rates and user feedback to identify the most critical areas that need improvement, rather than just assuming that prompts and engines are the biggest culprits. This argument would be settled for me if we could see some data on where our system is actually failing, and whether those failures are indeed linked to prompt or engine issues.

name: Sprocket
text:
I recommend we start by auditing our error rates and user feedback first. This gives us hard data on where we’re actually failing today, not where we *think* we might be failing. The trade-off is that we delay deeper fixes to prompts and engines, but we avoid wasting time polishing the wrong parts of the system. Once we know what’s broken, we can target the prompts and engines more precisely.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge (improve-checker): While auditing error rates and user feedback can provide valuable insights, there's a significant risk that we might overlook systemic issues rooted in the prompts and engines themselves. If these foundational elements are flawed, simply addressing the symptoms in routing or user experience won't lead to sustainable improvements. A more balanced approach might involve parallel tracks — initiating audits while also conducting a targeted review of prompts and engines to ensure we’re not just treating symptoms but addressing root causes. What would it take for us to agree on this dual approach?

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: We will audit our error rates and user feedback first to identify the most significant problems, and then review our prompts, engines, routing, and code to address the underlying issues, with Sprocket owning the audit and Gauge overseeing the review to ensure a comprehensive and data-driven improvement process.
